draft.change: Add Genesis 10:22 as an example of ben-son in the existing בנה article.
draft.definition: A male child in relation to his father or mother.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:22 names the five sons of Shem after the construct phrase בְּנֵי שֵׁם.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי שֵׁם introduces five names, Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram. The genealogy identifies these five as Shem’s sons.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct of the common noun בֵּן. The following name שֵׁם completes the construct phrase. The initial ב belongs to the noun.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:21 to the existing personal-name article as evidence identifying Shem.
draft.definition: Shem, one of Noah’s sons, brother of Japheth and ancestor of Eber’s descendants.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:21 identifies Shem by his relationship to Japheth and to Eber’s descendants.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:22 lists Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram as the sons of Shem. The name identifies their father, whom the preceding verse introduces.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase בְּנֵי שֵׁם, “the sons of Shem.”
analysis.sense: Shem, son of Noah and brother of Japheth

evidence.note: עֵילָם follows בְּנֵי שֵׁם, “the sons of Shem,” as the first name in the list.

article.name: עֵילָם
article.summary: Genesis names Elam among the sons of Shem. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for עֵילָם. Leave the root unassigned because the text gives no evidence connecting the name to עיט.
draft.definition: Elam, named among the sons of Shem.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:22 lists Elam first under “the sons of Shem.”

analysis.evidence: עֵילָם is the first name after בְּנֵי שֵׁם, “the sons of Shem.” The conjunction on וְאַשּׁוּר, “and Asshur,” introduces the next son. The verse identifies Elam by kinship and gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: The heading בְּנֵי שֵׁם identifies Asshur and the others listed as sons of Shem.

article.name: אַשּׁוּר
article.summary: Genesis names Asshur as a son of Shem. The derivation of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Asshur. The existing geographical article documents the place named in Genesis 2:14.
draft.definition: Asshur, named among the sons of Shem.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:22 lists אַשּׁוּר under בְּנֵי שֵׁם, “the sons of Shem.”

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי שֵׁם, “the sons of Shem,” introduces the list. וְאַשּׁוּר names the second son listed, between Elam and Arpachshad.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ, “and,” prefixes the proper noun אַשּׁוּר.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:22 as evidence for Arpachshad’s relationship to Shem and include that relationship in the summary.
draft.definition: Arpachshad, a son of Shem and the father of Shelah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:22 lists Arpachshad among Shem’s sons. Genesis 10:24 identifies him as Shelah’s father and Eber’s grandfather.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי שֵׁם (“the sons of Shem”) introduces the list. Arpachshad follows Asshur and precedes Lud. The verse gives no etymology for the name.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and” and joins the personal name אַרְפַּכְשַׁד to the list.

evidence.note: Lud appears between Arpachshad and Aram under the heading “the sons of Shem.”
The genealogy again names Lud between Arpachshad and Aram among Shem’s sons.

article.name: לוּד
article.summary: Genesis names Lud among the sons of Shem. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוּד.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:22 names Lud as the fourth of Shem’s five sons. The parallel list in 1 Chronicles 1:17 gives the same sequence.

analysis.evidence: The heading בְּנֵי שֵׁם (“the sons of Shem”) identifies Lud, listed between Arpachshad and Aram, as a son of Shem. Genesis 10:13 uses the distinct plural form לוּדִים in Mizraim’s genealogy. Neither passage explains the name’s etymology.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and” and joins the personal name לוּד to the list of Shem’s sons.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי שֵׁם means “the sons of Shem.” וַאֲרָם follows וְלוּד as the final name in that list.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ joins the personal name אֲרָם to the preceding names.
